subject: Burst lifecycle & session profile for Dedicated sizing — Nebula Dynamics
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@nebuladynamics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebuladynamics.com
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: initial traffic snapshot and SLA notes

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached are two files: nebuladynamics_traffic_samples.csv (7 days of anonymized traces) and our high-level SLA doc (sla_requirements.pdf). A short summary of what we care about:

- Peak concurrency target: 1,800 concurrent active sessions during US business peak (P95 of daily peak windows).
- Sustained baseline concurrency: ~220 sessions across the day.
- Burst events: estimated 3x baseline for 15–45 minutes during campaign launches (we expect about 6–8 of these per month).
- Typical prompt mix: ~65% short prompts (5–40 tokens), 25% medium (40–180 tokens), 10% long (180–1,200 tokens).
- Average response lengths: short prompts -> 20 tokens, medium -> 120 tokens, long -> 600 tokens.
- Session behavior: many short-turn chat sessions (1–6 turns) and occasional long-running generation flows for batch processing. KV-cache reuse expected for multi-turn chat, but batch jobs are stateless.
- Model target: evaluating Llama2-70B and a trimmed 33B variant; open to your recommendations on quantization/tradeoffs.

Two asks: 1) Can you confirm what info you need to give us a recommended dedicated pool size (GPUs / vCPU / memory)? 2) Can you run a runbook/workshop to validate burst sizing assumptions next week?

Appreciate it — Amit

--
Amit Shah
Head of Platform Engineering
Nebula Dynamics

Attachments: nebuladynamics_traffic_samples.csv (csv), sla_requirements.pdf (pdf)

Hi Amit — thanks for the files and the concise summary. Quick notes and a couple clarifying questions so we can size confidently:

1) Clarifications we need to produce a recommended dedicated pool:
   - P95/P99 arrival rates during peak windows (tokens/sec or requests/sec), not just concurrency. If you can compute 1-minute QPS and 5-minute QPS percentiles that helps.
   - Breakdown of prompt length distribution by percentiles (10/50/90) rather than just buckets if possible.
   - Typical KV-cache hit rate for multi-turn chat sessions (%).
   - Fraction of calls requiring streaming vs. synchronous complete-response semantics.

2) Model details: if you expect to run both 70B and 33B variants in production, do you plan to route some traffic to the trimmed model for cost-sensitive paths? That affects pool mix.

3) Sizing workshop: we can run a 30–45 minute workshop to go over burst scenarios and run a quick probabilistic burst sampler; proposed slots Tue/Wed next week (Mar 23/24 10–12 PT). Which works for you?

Technical note: CC'ing Karhik (inference) and Marissa (capacity) so they can weigh in on KV/cache and pack/quant options.

Thanks,
Tessa

Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Amit Shah <amit@nebuladynamics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial traffic snapshot and SLA notes

Amit / Tessa — quick technical context from the runtime side:

- KV-cache: for multi-turn chat, KV-cache hit ratio is the single biggest influencer on amortized GPU work per session. If your multi-turn sessions average 3+ turns with consistent context, we can assume 55–70% effective reuse; if turns are mostly unique contexts, plan for <30%.
- Model selection: Llama2-70B will demand ~350–420 GB GPU memory when unquantized; with Q8_INT8 quantization and tiled attention we can target deployment on 80GB-class GPUs with ~1.1x latency overhead vs fp16 in exchange for substantial throughput gains. 33B trimmed variants are much cheaper—good for cost-sensitive routing.
- Suggestion: hybrid pool: majority of baseline capacity on 33B-quantized for cost; a smaller hot pool of 70B capacity for high-quality paths or longer generations. Autoscaling for burst windows with pre-warmed instances reduces cold-start pressure.

For the sizing exercise please provide observed P95 token-emission rate for long responses (your 600-token cases) – that drives KV cache pressure and memory residency.

Happy to run a quick local simulation during the workshop.

—Karthik
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@nebuladynamics.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial traffic snapshot and SLA notes

Amit — high-level sizing approach attached (tidal-sizer-v1.xlsx). A few pragmatic anchors so you know what we'll deliver after the workshop:

- Baseline recommendation (based on the numbers you provided and assuming 60% KV reuse for chat):
   * 6 x 80GB GPUs for baseline (33B quantized mix), estimated sustained concurrency headroom ~260 sessions with conservative packing.
   * Hot pool for quality (70B quantized on 80GB GPUs): 2 x 80GB GPUs pre-warmed to handle 300 concurrent sessions in the hot path during short bursts.
   * Autoscale policy for bursts: allow +4 GPUs for short bursts (15–45m) with pre-warm windows of 3–5 minutes.

- Cost/quality trade: shifting 40% of medium-length traffic to the 33B trimmed model reduces token cost ~35% but increases median latency by ~10–20ms. We include quantization sensitivity in the spreadsheet.

- Risk notes: if KV-cache reuse is <30% or if long 600-token responses are >P95 frequent, we should increase the hot pool and memory headroom — we can test this in the workshop with your traces.

Next steps I propose:
1) Run the 45-minute sizing workshop (hands-on with your trace file) — we’ll run the probabilistic burst sampler and a quick simulation to validate the autoscale knobs.
2) Produce a committed-pool proposal and an optional pilot plan (2-week pilot with telemetry hooks) and an SOW for procurement.

Ben — I’ve attached an initial committed-pool cost snapshot; can you help produce the SOW draft if Amit confirms pilot?

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
